summary: Fresh read-only diagnostics proved PGRST002 is a downstream symptom, not a Tele-only schema-cache defect. The Supabase project reports ACTIVE_HEALTHY in project metadata, but live PostgreSQL startup repeatedly fails with SQLSTATE 53100 and 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp.*: No space left on device'. No destructive storage mutation was attempted. Recovery now requires Supabase storage/platform authority to restore usable disk capacity before PostgREST and the existing Tele two-client verifier can be rerun.
tests: CONFIRMED_PGRST002_PERSISTS: live PostgREST responses returned HTTP 503 / PostgREST; error=PGRST002 across multiple unrelated REST endpoints and auth modes.
CONFIRMED_DATABASE_ROOT_CAUSE: PostgreSQL startup logs repeatedly emitted FATAL SQLSTATE 53100 with 'No space left on device' while writing pg_wal/xlogtemp files.
CONFIRMED_RESTART_LOOP: repeated startup failures were observed seconds apart through 2026-10-01T21:29:26Z.
PASS_NO_DESTRUCTIVE_MUTATION: no DELETE, VACUUM, pruning, destructive migration, backup restore, table mutation or Tele backend mutation was performed.
NOT_RUN_TWO_CLIENT_REVERIFY: backend is not healthy, so pairing/remote commands/tv.state were correctly not claimed as verified.
unresolved: Restore usable Supabase database disk capacity through an authorized platform/storage owner, then confirm PostgreSQL exits the 53100 startup loop and PostgREST recovers before rerunning Tele two-client verification.
